name: Huddleston Hall
use: Hamel Honors and Scholars College: offices, classrooms, lounge, study 'huddle' spaces, ballroom function space
builtText: Opened 1919 as the Commons; renamed Huddleston Hall in 1963
architect: Eric T. Huddleston (original); Engelberth Construction (2023-24 renovation)
statusNote: Home of the Hamel Honors and Scholars College since 2024

renovations.what: Historic-preservation renovation for the Hamel Honors and Scholars College: full 2nd floor, partial 1st and 3rd, new elevator, life-safety and energy systems, ADA upgrades, new 3,500 sf two-storey accessible entrance addition, roof shingles, parking moved to rear; opened September 29, 2024

facts.text: Opened in 1919 as the Commons, the first campus dining hall; wartime material restrictions delayed it a year. The third floor was built as a men's dormitory but housed women.
It served as the dining hall until spring 2003, when Holloway Commons replaced it; its dining room became a ballroom used as function space.
Named Huddleston Hall since 1963 for campus architect Eric T. Huddleston, who designed it in a restrained Colonial Revival style with white columns and Palladian windows.
The 40,000 sf, four-storey building was renovated as the home of the Hamel Honors and Scholars College, with a new 3,500 sf two-storey accessible entrance addition.
The renovation was enabled by a $20 million gift from Dana Hamel; the ribbon was cut September 29, 2024.
The renovated ballroom has high ceilings and lots of natural light from half-round windows.

photos.caption: Three-storey brick facade with dormers and arched windows behind trees (2013, before the renovation)

engelberth.title: Huddleston Hall, Hamel Honors and Scholars College

verdict: The 1919 Commons, restored in 2024 for the Honors College; its old dining room is now a sunlit ballroom students love.
notes: Category corrected from 'student-life' to 'academic': it now houses the Honors College's offices and classrooms. The licensed 2013 photo shows a brick Colonial Revival block with a stone-capped balustrade, dormers and arched first-floor windows; I can't confirm which facade it shows, and it predates the 2024 glass entrance addition. The cost of the renovation itself is not published (the $20M gift also funded the Hamel Scholars endowment). The ~1994 $5.5M restructuring and the Harriman design credit in the old row were not verified.
judgeNotes: Photo shows a handsome Colonial Revival front with dormers; ballroom described as high and bright. Exterior trimmed to 7 to match Congreve and Hetzel.
